strengths: Consistent dispatch-table pattern (CONTROL_FLOW_ACTIONS, ERROR_HANDLING_DETECTORS, FUNCTION_LENGTH_RULES, DECLARATION_KIND_COUNTER) keeps visitor cyclomatic complexity at 1-2 everywhere.

Clear tiered decomposition — buildFeatureVector delegates to computeBaseFeatures / computeAdvancedFeatures / computeStructuralFeatures by feature family (F1-F5, F6-F10, F11-F16), and naming is self-documenting end to end.
weaknesses: computeBaseFeatures(metrics, topMeta, nonEmptyLines) never uses nonEmptyLines — dead parameter left from a refactor; and extractFeatures computes nonEmptyLines twice (once inside buildFeatureVector, once right after).

Two separate full-tree AST walks (walk.full in gatherNodeMetrics + walk.ancestor in computeMaxNestingDepth) could be a single pass; measureCallChainDepth uses an awkward Array.from({length}).reduce pattern where a while loop would be clearer.
reasoning: Above-average module, clearly refactored with intent. The dispatch-table approach is applied consistently and pays off — cyclomatic complexity stays low and each visitor owns exactly one metric. Naming, decomposition, and function length are all strong. The ceiling is pulled down by a dead parameter in computeBaseFeatures, a recomputed nonEmptyLines, two full-tree walks that could be one, and a few hard-coded scoring weights (0.40/0.35/0.25) that should have been extracted as named constants like OVERRUN_FLOOR_SCORE was. GOOD, not excellent.
